CodeForge is a new online platform designed to help beginners learn programming through hands-on projects rather than passive video lessons. Each course walks you through building a real application, step by step, with instant feedback on your code.

Courses cover popular languages including Python, JavaScript, and Java, with new content added monthly. A free trial gives you access to the first three lessons of any course, no credit card required.

Subscribers also gain access to a community forum where they can ask questions and get help from more experienced programmers.

This year's Riverside City Marathon drew a record 12,000 participants, surpassing last year's total by nearly 20 percent. Race organizers credit the growth to a new scenic route along the waterfront and expanded categories for walkers and wheelchair racers.

Proceeds from registration fees will go toward funding youth sports programs throughout the city, with organizers estimating this year's event will raise over $150,000. 

Despite the larger crowd, organizers reported the race ran smoothly, with only minor delays at the starting line due to the increased number of runners.

The county agricultural department launched a new grant program this week aimed at helping small family farms adopt sustainable farming practices. Grants of up to $10,000 will be available to cover costs such as soil testing, drip irrigation systems, and cover crop seeds.

Farms with fewer than 200 acres are eligible to apply, and priority will be given to farms that have been in operation for at least five years. The application window opens next month and will remain open for eight weeks.

Program coordinators say the initiative aims to help local farms remain competitive while reducing their environmental impact.

Roastworks Coffee, a regional café chain with 18 locations, announced this week that it will offer all employees the opportunity to become part owners of the company through a new employee stock ownership plan. Employees who have worked at the company for at least one year will be automatically enrolled.

Company founder Diane Okafor said the decision reflects her belief that employees who helped build the business should share in its success. The plan will gradually transfer 20 percent of company ownership to employees over the next decade.

Industry analysts say the move is relatively rare among small regional chains and could help Roastworks retain staff in a competitive hiring market.
